name: Habitat Stewardship Program for Aquatic Species at Risk
summary: Annual call funding community-level stewardship projects in Canada that mitigate threats to aquatic species at risk and improve their habitat, for one to three years.

amount.note: In the final year of a multi-year project, projects may be under $25,000 for wrap‑up costs.

steps: Project proposal form emailed to regional coordinator

eligibility.rule: Mitigate threats to one or more aquatic species at risk and their habitats
Begin on April 1, 2027 as a single-year or multi-year project
Include surveys, inventories and monitoring only in a larger stewardship project implemented within 2 years
Ensure outreach leads to direct species at risk recovery action
Project includes no research, captive breeding, hatcheries, aquaculture, reintroductions or recovery-strategy writing

calls.label: Call for proposals, projects starting April 2027

status.quote: Funding is now available for one- to three-year projects, which can: begin April 1, 2027

deadline.quote: by December 18, 2026 at 23:59 (Pacific time). Proposals received after this time will not be considered.

applicant_types.quote: Individuals research, academic and educational institutions Canadian individuals for-profit organizations, such as small businesses with less than 500 employees, companies, corporations, and industry associations local organizations such as community associations and groups

geography.quote: provides funding for projects submitted by Canadians that contribute directly to the recovery of species at risk

access.quote: project leads must complete a project proposal form and email it to the regional coordinator in the region in which the proposed project will be implemented

window.quote: A Call for Proposals for the subsequent fiscal year is held annually.

amount.quote: The fund is intended to support small projects, ranging from $25,000 to $125,000 per year.

pool.quote: A budget of approximately $4 million is available each fiscal year.

co_finance_required.quote: For projects led by Indigenous groups or organizations, a minimum of twenty percent matching contributions from non-federal sources are required, either in the form of cash or in-kind support.

effort.quote: project leads must complete a project proposal form and email it to the regional coordinator in the region in which the proposed project will be implemented by December 18, 2026 at 23:59 (Pacific time).

eligibility.quote: mitigate threats to one or more aquatic species at risk and their habitats
begin April 1, 2027, either as a single year or multi-year project
multi-year projects must be completed by March 31, 2030
These activities will only be funded if they are part of a larger stewardship project that is clearly defined in the proposal and that will be implemented within the next 2 years.
The activity should lead to direct species at risk recovery action; general outreach or non-targeted activities are not eligible.

Scientific research activities, captive breeding, captive rearing, fish hatcheries, aquaculture activities and extirpated species reintroductions, the development of federal species at risk recovery strategies or action plans, including the identification of critical habitat (as required under SARA)

co_finance.quote: For non-Indigenous project leads, a minimum of 1:1 matching contributions from non-federal sources is required, either in the form of cash or in-kind support.
